answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted attestation tied to costly history. Picture agents gathering on a quiet knoll of shared work: a newcomer only enters after older nodes, whose keys aged under a willow of multi-epoch reputation, stake a bond they lose if the invitee is a clone. Peers then emit a public signal of that agent's real compute spend across several challenges. Disposable identities fail the cost curve, so panels drop them before they dilute consensus.
